title: Earlier BATS water types fit the 2016-2025 five-property mean with zero to 19.87 micromol/kg of added oxygen use
abstract: BATS oxygen on density 26.5 fell by 10.85 micromol/kg between 1989-1998 and 2016-2025 in a joint five-property sample. We tested whether the later state requires added oxygen use beyond arbitrary mixtures of earlier individual bottles. Linear programs preserve Absolute Salinity and Conservative Temperature and fit oxygen, nitrate plus nitrite and phosphate with a fixed O:N:P reaction ratio of -170:16:1. Exact fits of the later mean using 650 earlier bottles in density 26.4-26.6 permit every added-use value from zero to 19.87 micromol/kg. A wider density range permits zero to 36.93. Stored primal and dual checks support the sharp finite-library endpoints. Zero minima survive early-year deletion, tail removal, distributed source weights and late target resampling at stated error bounds. An earlier-year validation has zero minima in all ten years. Thus these five properties do not require a positive added-use term, even with a narrow density library. This does not show that mixing caused the loss. The source weights have no transport or mass-supply constraint, and earlier bottles already contain oxygen-use histories. The result limits process attribution from hydrography and nutrients alone; it does not separate age from respiration rate.

display.caption: Annual tolerance bounds and exact mean bounds on extra oxygen use under earlier observed source libraries. The ranges are conditional mathematical bounds, not confidence intervals.
